{"design":"## State, 2026-11-26

Done, and needing no openmls change:

- mimi-mls wire::WireFormats: the body of mls-extensions-11 §6.1's two
  extensions, with the 0x0007 and 0x0008 codepoints and a 64-entry cap.
- Observer::required_wire_formats reads it from the GroupContext, through
  Extension::Unknown.
- Member::create_requiring puts it in a new group. Additive: create
  delegates with an empty list, so its 80 call sites are untouched.
- The hub refuses a room whose required_wire_formats names the
  semiprivate format and lists no external receiver
  (HubError::MissingExternalReceivers), which is §3's second condition
  and was deferred when the first was written.
- Every leaf advertises extension type 0x0008, without which no room
  could require any format at all (decision mimid-1wgh.4.79.10).

Not done, and blocked on an approval rather than on work:

- A member cannot SEND a SemiPrivateMessage. That needs a WireFormat
  variant (0x0011) in the openmls patch branch, behind a feature, after
  the targeted-messages-draft precedent, plus access to the sender's own
  handshake ratchet to derive the key and nonce §3.1 calls for.
  AGENTS.md requires Mark to approve each write to that branch; the
  approval of 2026-11-26 covered exporting CommitIn and
  FramedContentAuthData, and is not being read as open-ended.
- mimi-protocol accepting SemiPrivateMessage in UpdateRequest and
  FanoutMessage (protocol-07 §5.3, §5.5) follows the sending side,
  because there is nothing to carry until a member can build one.
- Leaves will advertise mls_semiprivate_message in
  supported_wire_formats only once sending works. Advertising it before
  then invites a room mimid would fail in.

What the hub can do today: read a SemiPrivateMessage another
implementation sends, and refuse a room that requires the format without
naming a receiver. That is enough for interop testing against an
implementation that sends them."}
